sections.h2: Why color looks different once it is on your wall
body: Almost everyone has had this happen: a color looks perfect on a one-inch chip at the store, and once it is on the wall it is too blue, too yellow, or too dark. Florida makes this worse. Our sun is bright and high for most of the year, and it bounces off green lawns and tree canopy before it comes through the windows. Cool grays drift toward blue. Warm whites go creamy or even yellow on a west wall late in the afternoon. A beige that looked neutral can turn pink next to terracotta tile.

A paint color consultation fixes this by testing colors where they will actually live. This page covers our standalone consultation, which you can book for any project, whether or not we do the painting. If you already know you want the whole interior repainted and the color work built in, see our interior painting with color consultation package instead.

sections.h2: Start with what is not changing
body: A good palette is built outward from the things you are keeping. Inside, that means flooring, countertops, backsplash tile, cabinets, stone fireplaces, and large furniture. Outside, it means roof color, brick or stone accents, pavers, and the color of the screen enclosure. We look at all of that first, then narrow paint options to the ones that work with it.

From there, the session moves room by room or elevation by elevation. We usually aim for one main wall color that flows through connected spaces, one consistent trim color, and a small number of accents for rooms that can carry them.
bullets: In-home or virtual session, about an hour
Review of fixed finishes, lighting, and how each room is used
Shortlist of colors for walls, ceilings, trim, doors, and accents
Full-size drawdown boards you can move around the room
A written list of colors, formulas, and suggested sheens

sections.h2: Large drawdowns instead of tiny chips
body: Instead of painting small swatches on your wall, we bring full-size drawdown boards: real paint, two coats, on a large card. You can move them from wall to wall and look at them in morning light, afternoon light, and under lamps at night. Living with a board for a day tells you more than an hour in the store.
You keep the boards and the color list whether or not you hire us for the painting. If you are matching an existing color, we can match from a chip, a cabinet door, or a leftover can.

sections.h2: Common color problems we help solve
body: Most consultations start with a specific frustration. A living room painted gray that now reads blue and cold. A kitchen where the wall color fights the granite. A hallway so dark it needs the lights on at noon. A house where every room is a different beige and nothing connects. Or a homeowner about to list a house who wants neutral colors that photograph well and appeal to the most buyers.

In each case, the fix is usually smaller than people expect: shifting the undertone, adjusting the light reflectance, or picking a trim white that stops clashing with the cabinets. Seeing the options side by side on large boards makes those differences obvious in a way that chips never do.

sections.h2: Exterior colors, HOAs, and historic homes
body: Exterior colors carry more weight because they are hard to change and everyone sees them. Strong sun washes out lighter colors, so an exterior shade often needs to be a step deeper than you would choose indoors to look right from the street. Very dark colors on sun-facing walls absorb a lot of heat, which is worth discussing for stucco and for doors.

In neighborhoods with an HOA, we help you pick a scheme that fits the approved palette and give you the color names and samples you need for the application. For older homes, our article on historic paint colors in Gainesville covers schemes that suit bungalows and early 20th-century houses. Once the colors are set, our exterior painting crews can carry them through.

Color consultations are not only for homes. Offices, shops, churches, and rental properties benefit from a standard palette too: a durable wall color that hides scuffs, one trim color, and an accent that ties to signage or brand colors. For landlords and property managers, a written color standard means every unit or suite can be repainted to match later without guesswork.

For more ideas before you book, read our guide to interior paint colors that work in Florida homes. We offer consultations across the region; local details are on our Gainesville color consultation and Ocala color consultation pages.

faqs.q: Why does paint look different on my wall than on the chip?
faqs.a: Chips are small and viewed under store lighting. On a wall, the color is much larger, reflects off your floors and furniture, and changes with Florida daylight, which is bright and often filtered through green landscaping. Testing large samples in place is the reliable fix.

faqs.q: Can I book a color consultation without hiring you to paint?
faqs.a: Yes. The consultation stands on its own, and you keep the drawdown boards and the written color list whether or not we do the painting.

faqs.q: How do I pick exterior colors that my HOA will approve?
faqs.a: Start with the HOA's approved palette and pick a combination that suits your roof and stone or brick. We help narrow the options and provide the color names and samples you need for the application.

faqs.q: Do you help with commercial color schemes?
faqs.a: Yes. We help offices, retail spaces, churches, and rental properties set a standard palette, including colors tied to signage or brand standards.
